newsitem.title: USA: Brent crude ends up slightly in U.S. aftermarket.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude ends up slightly in U.S. aftermarket.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil started out strong then dropped, ending up slightly in the U.S. aftermarket on Wednesday, traders said.
Early on, a full boat of September Brent changed hands at $18.54 a barrel, up 11 cents from the IPE settlement.
Partial cargoes then traded at much lower levels. Two cargoes totalling 150 lots traded at $18.43, two more totalling 200 lots traded at $18.45 and one of 150 lots traded at $18.46.
The outright price went out at $18.43-47 a barrel.
August/September Brent was assessed at plus 16-17 cents a barrel, while September/October was pegged at minus five to three cents.
